## GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus)

### URL construction

GEO groups accessions by replacing the last 3 digits with `nnn`:

- `GSE165252` → parent dir `GSE165nnn`
- `GPL570` → parent dir `GPLnnn`
- `GSE9348` → parent dir `GSE9nnn`

Common download URLs:

| Resource            | URL pattern                                                                                            |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Series matrix       | `https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/{prefix}/{accession}/matrix/{accession}_series_matrix.txt.gz` |
| Supplementary files | `https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/{prefix}/{accession}/suppl/`                                  |
| Platform annotation | `https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/platforms/{prefix}/{accession}/annot/{accession}.annot.gz`           |
| SOFT metadata       | `https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc={accession}&targ=self&form=text&view=data`         |
| Sample metadata     | `https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc={accession}&targ=gsm&form=text&view=data`          |

### Probe-to-gene mapping

- Try `annot.gz` first.
- If unavailable, fetch the platform table from `https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc={GPL_ID}&targ=self&form=text&view=data` and parse the `!platform_table_begin` / `!platform_table_end` section.
- Avoid `_family.soft.gz` when the platform table provides the mapping.

## NCBI eUtils (shared by GEO, ClinVar, dbSNP, RefSeq, GenBank)

Base URLs:

- Search: `https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi`
- Summary: `https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi`
- Fetch: `https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi`

Always use `retmode=json` for esearch/esummary. Add 0.4s delay between calls to avoid rate limiting. Use `&api_key=` from NCBI_API_KEY env var if available.

## ClinVar

ClinVar uses NCBI eUtils with database `clinvar`.

```python
# Search by gene + clinical significance
params = {
    "db": "clinvar",
    "term": 'SHH[GENE] AND "pathogenic"[CLNSIG]',
    "retmode": "json",
    "retmax": "100",
}
# Search by known Variation ID
params = {"db": "clinvar", "term": "1703527[VariationID]", "retmode": "json"}
```

⚠️ **Position-based search** (`[CHRPOS37]`, `[CHRPOS]`) often returns 0 results
in eSearch even for valid positions. If you need to find variants by genomic
coordinates, search by gene name instead and filter by position client-side,
or use the NCBI Variation Services SPDI endpoint:
`https://api.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/variation/v0/spdi/NC_000007.13:155593769:1:T`

Combining `[CLNSIG]` with `[CLNORIGIN]` can return no results even when matching variants exist. Retry with fewer filters and filter client-side.

Fetch details with efetch: `db=clinvar&rettype=clinvarset&retmode=xml`.

## dbSNP

Search via eUtils (`db=snp`).

```python
# Filter by gene + clinical significance (use exact value with quotes)
params = {
    "db": "snp",
    "term": 'SHH[GENE] AND "likely-pathogenic"[Clinical_Significance] AND homo sapiens[ORGN]',
    "retmode": "json",
    "retmax": "100",
}
```

⚠️ dbSNP does not have a "somatic origin" field in eSearch. To find somatic
variants, search dbSNP by gene + clinical significance, then cross-reference
each result against ClinVar (`db=clinvar`) for origin information.

Use esummary (`db=snp`) with the returned IDs for variant details (position,
gene, functional class, clinical significance).

The Gateway to Research (GTR) API allows you to get the data used to show content on <https://gtr.ukri.org/>.

The GTR API is accessed via [HTTP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypertext_Transfer_Protocol) and returns data in a [JSON](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JSON) format. The [reference documentation](https://gtr.ukri.org/swagger) shows the endpoints and the response format.

## What you can do with this API

The GTR API allows you to query data on all the research and innovation funded by UK Research and Innovation (UKRI). For a project you could access the organisation awarded funding, the people doing the work and any outcomes or publications resulting from that piece of research or innovation.

By combining the data on GTR with other datasets from other sources you could make new insights.

## What you can’t do with this API

The content within this API is limited to pages hosted on <https://gtr.ukri.org/> and does not include other websites that are subdomains of <https://ukri.org/>.

This API only includes the pages on GTR that are available as HTML.

You can [access historic content from GTR through the National Archives](https://webarchive.nationalarchives.gov.uk/ukgwa/*/http://gtr.ukri.org).

# RSC Tokenomics

The following section describes ResearchCoin token design and major token metrics, such as the distribution chart, emission schedule, and token burns.

ResearchCoin tokenomics has been designed based on token engineering principles centered around the concept of the [Web3 Sustainability Loop](https://blog.oceanprotocol.com/the-web3-sustainability-loop-b2a4097a36e). This implies that the primary focus has always been on growing the ecosystem while ensuring its long-term self-sustainability.

In this context, RSC tokens are distributed gradually to contributors who add value to the project. This approach not only aligns incentives for those committed to the long-term vision of ResearchHub but also provides the team with a longer runway to iterate and discover the most effective mechanisms for catalyzing growth and converting it into value for science.

Examples of such iterations include the Editor program, the Incentivized Peer Review program, and Microgrants. In each of these cases, RSC tokens are disbursed to contributors capable of creating value for the broader scientific community. This value is then captured by the platform through increased user adoption, subsequently generating more value for the platform through heightened awareness and the utilization of services and products offered by ResearchHub.

This set of utilities not only enhances the overall value proposition of RSC but also fosters a dynamic and engaged community. By doing so, the ResearchHub Foundation ensures that RSC becomes a key driver for active participation and collaboration within the scientific community and aims to establish a set of positive incentives capable of creating value for all network participants, thus helping accelerate the pace of scientific research.
